question: Do you maintain an inventory of every AI system, model and AI-enabled feature used to deliver or support the services you provide to us?
alternatives: Provide a list of all AI and machine learning components in your solution.
Describe the AI systems that are part of the service, including third-party models.
business_concern: Customer needs to know where AI touches its data and processes to govern its own AI risk.
risk_addressed: Unknown AI use creates unassessed data, accuracy and security exposure.

question: Does your AI inventory include AI used internally to build, test and operate the service, such as AI coding agents and AI operations assistants, and not only AI features exposed to customers?
alternatives: Do your developers use AI coding assistants? Which ones?
Is generative AI used in your software development lifecycle?
business_concern: Customers increasingly ask how vendor software is produced, because AI-written code and AI operators change the risk profile.
risk_addressed: Internal AI use with access to source code, secrets or production goes unassessed.

question: For each AI use, which data classes can it access, which provider hosts the model, and which model version is in use?
business_concern: Data exposure depends on what each AI component can read and where it is processed.
risk_addressed: Customer data reaches a model provider or model version the customer has not assessed.

question: How do you detect and prevent unapproved AI tools (shadow AI) receiving customer data from your personnel or contractors?
alternatives: Do you block or monitor employee use of public generative AI services?
business_concern: Unsanctioned AI tools are a common data leakage path.
risk_addressed: Confidential customer data entered into consumer AI tools with training-permissive terms.

question: When a model version, provider, prompt or tool changes, how quickly is the AI inventory updated, and how is completeness verified?
business_concern: A stale inventory gives false assurance.
risk_addressed: Changes to AI behavior go unrecorded and unreviewed.

question: Can you give us a customer-specific list of the AI components and AI providers that process our data?
business_concern: Customer must record vendor AI use in its own AI inventory and regulatory filings.
risk_addressed: Customer cannot meet its own inventory or disclosure obligations.

question: Do you have a formally approved policy governing the development, procurement and use of AI? Who approved it and when was it last reviewed?
alternatives: Please provide your AI governance policy.
Does your organization have an acceptable use policy for artificial intelligence?
business_concern: A formal policy shows management commitment and sets enforceable rules.
risk_addressed: AI use is governed by individual judgment with no accountable standard.

question: Who is the accountable executive for AI risk, and how does AI risk reach senior management or the board?
business_concern: Accountability must sit with a named person with authority.
risk_addressed: AI risk decisions are made without accountable ownership.

question: What rules govern your personnel entering our confidential data into AI tools, and how are those rules enforced technically?
business_concern: Customer data handling rules must extend to AI tools.
risk_addressed: Customer data disclosed to AI providers outside contractual protections.

history.change: Added real-world alternative wording from DD-QNR-001 topic 3 and source reference(s) SRC-Q-TRUIST-TPISS, SRC-Q-MS-MIN-SECURITY-STANDARDS (maps-to)

alternatives: Are your personnel prohibited from entering our data into third-party or open-source generative AI tools, and how is that prohibition enforced?

question: What AI literacy training do your personnel and agent operators receive, and how is completion tracked?
business_concern: Staff who use or oversee AI must understand its limits, including automation bias.
risk_addressed: Untrained operators over-trust AI outputs or misuse AI tools.
regulatory_authority: EU AI Act national market surveillance authorities
answer_scope_note: Article 4 applies to providers and deployers of AI systems within the AI Act's scope; applicability to Echelon depends on EU exposure, which is not established.

question: How are exceptions to your AI policy requested, approved, time-limited and recorded?
business_concern: Exceptions are where policy fails in practice.
risk_addressed: Permanent undocumented exceptions erode the policy.

question: Have you aligned your AI risk management to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, including the Generative AI Profile? Can you share the mapping?
alternatives: Which AI risk management framework does your organization follow?
business_concern: A recognized framework gives the customer a common reference for completeness.
risk_addressed: Material AI risk categories are not considered.

question: Are you certified to ISO/IEC 42001, and if not, do you plan to be? What scope and timeline?
alternatives: Do you hold any AI-related certifications?
business_concern: Certification offers independent assurance of an AI management system.
risk_addressed: Customer relies on unverified vendor claims about AI governance.

question: Has any independent party assessed your AI governance or AI controls, for example a SOC 2 examination covering AI agents or an ISO/IEC 42001 audit?
business_concern: Independent assessment distinguishes operating controls from intentions.
risk_addressed: AI controls described in questionnaires are not operating.

question: Do you map your AI controls to the CSA AI Controls Matrix or a similar control catalog that we can compare across vendors?
business_concern: Comparable control catalogs speed vendor assessment.
risk_addressed: Inconsistent vendor AI assessments across the customer portfolio.

question: Before deploying an AI capability, do you perform a documented risk assessment covering accuracy, security, privacy, bias and misuse? Who approves it?
alternatives: Describe your AI risk assessment process.
How do you assess risks of new AI use cases?
business_concern: AI risks should be assessed before exposure, not after an incident.
risk_addressed: Harmful or insecure AI capabilities reach production unassessed.

question: Do you assess the impact of your AI systems on individuals affected by them, such as donors, advisors, grantees and employees?
business_concern: AI that affects people can cause harms that a security-only review misses.
risk_addressed: Unfair or opaque treatment of individuals by automated processes.

history.change: Replaced SRC-COLORADO-AI-ACT with SRC-COLORADO-SB26-189 (SB 26-189, signed 2026-05-14, repealed and reenacted the Colorado AI Act as an automated decision-making technology law)

question: Is AI used to make, or to be a substantial factor in, any decision about an individual's eligibility, access to services, financial outcome or employment?
business_concern: Consequential automated decisions attract specific legal duties and higher scrutiny.
risk_addressed: Unlawful or unfair automated decisions and the liability that follows.
regulatory_authority: Colorado Attorney General; EU data protection authorities
answer_scope_note: Legal duties arise only if AI is a substantial factor in such decisions; Unbound design intends that it is not, which requires counsel confirmation.

history.change: Replaced SRC-COLORADO-AI-ACT with SRC-COLORADO-SB26-189 (SB 26-189, signed 2026-05-14, repealed and reenacted the Colorado AI Act as an automated decision-making technology law)

question: How do you test automated matching or scoring, for example sanctions name matching, for higher false-alert rates on particular name origins or groups?
business_concern: Disparate false alerts burden specific donors and grantees and can be discriminatory.
risk_addressed: Systematic delay or denial for people with names of certain origins.

question: What events cause an AI risk assessment to be repeated, for example a model change, new data source, new use or incident?
business_concern: Risk changes when the model, data or use changes.
risk_addressed: Assessment becomes stale while the AI behavior changes.

question: Which third-party AI model providers do you use, and what due diligence did you perform on each before use?
alternatives: List the foundation models and AI vendors used in your product.
business_concern: AI providers are critical vendors with access to customer content.
risk_addressed: Reliance on a provider with weak security, poor data terms or unstable service.

question: Do you obtain and review SOC 2 or equivalent assurance reports from your AI providers, and how do you implement their complementary user entity controls?
business_concern: Provider assurance only holds if the user entity controls are operated.
risk_addressed: Gaps between provider controls and Echelon's assumed controls.

question: Before adopting a model, do you review its documentation, such as system cards, evaluation results and known limitations, against your intended use?
business_concern: Model fitness depends on documented limitations.
risk_addressed: A model is used outside its demonstrated competence.

question: How do you detect and control provider-initiated model updates or deprecations so that model behavior does not change in production without your review?
business_concern: Silent model changes alter outputs without any vendor change record.
risk_addressed: Regression in accuracy or safety after an unannounced provider update.

question: If you use open-weight or third-party models, how do you assess their license and acceptable use terms against your commercial use?
business_concern: License breaches can force removal of a component the service depends on.
risk_addressed: Legal exposure or forced replacement of a model.

question: Do the AI providers you use retain prompts and outputs that contain our data, and for how long?
alternatives: What is your AI vendor's data retention policy for inputs and outputs?
business_concern: Retained prompts extend the footprint of customer data.
risk_addressed: Customer data persists at a provider beyond the customer's retention rules.

question: Is our data used by you or any AI provider to train, fine-tune or improve models? Is that prohibited by contract?
alternatives: Will customer data be used to train AI models?
Do you opt out of model training with your AI providers?
Will the contract state that our data may not be used to train or improve any AI model, yours or a provider's, without our written consent?
business_concern: Customers commonly prohibit training on their data to protect confidentiality and IP.
risk_addressed: Customer or donor data memorized and exposed through a model.

history.change: Added real-world alternative wording from DD-QNR-001 topic 2 and source reference(s) SRC-Q-NYDFS-IL-20251021-TPSP, SRC-Q-ACLU-GENAI-VENDOR-Q, SRC-Q-FSISAC-GENAI-VENDOR-GUIDE (maps-to)

question: Do AI provider terms allow provider staff to review prompts for abuse monitoring, and have you obtained zero-retention or opt-out terms where available?
business_concern: Human review by a provider is a disclosure of customer content.
risk_addressed: Unexpected human access to confidential donor or financial data.

question: Will you use our data to train, tune or evaluate your own models, agents or prompts, including building evaluation sets?
business_concern: Evaluation and tuning uses are often overlooked in no-training commitments.
risk_addressed: Customer data reused across customers through evaluation sets or tuned prompts.

question: Have you determined whether any of your AI systems are high-risk under the EU AI Act, and whether you act as provider or deployer?
business_concern: EU AI Act obligations depend on risk class and role.
risk_addressed: Non-compliance with EU AI Act obligations that flow to customers.
regulatory_authority: EU AI Act national market surveillance authorities
answer_scope_note: Applies only if Echelon places AI systems on the EU market or their output is used in the EU; no EU exposure is established. As amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Annex III high-risk obligations apply from 2027-12-02 and Annex I high-risk obligations from 2028-08-02.

history.change: Added SRC-EU-AI-OMNIBUS-2026 and the amended high-risk application dates to the scope note

question: Does Colorado's automated decision-making technology law (SB 26-189, which repealed and reenacted the Colorado AI Act) apply to any of your systems as a developer or deployer, and what documentation will you provide to us as deployer?
business_concern: Colorado imposes documentation duties on developers of covered automated decision-making technology from 2027-01-01, and duties on deployers.
risk_addressed: Customer cannot meet deployer obligations without developer documentation.
open_questions: Does any Unbound function materially influence a consequential decision about a Colorado individual, such as a decision on financial services, under SB 26-189?

history.change: Replaced SRC-COLORADO-AI-ACT with SRC-COLORADO-SB26-189 (SB 26-189, signed 2026-05-14, repealed and reenacted the Colorado AI Act as an automated decision-making technology law); question reworded with the former wording kept as an alternative; SB 24-205 section locators removed because the reenacted law was not mapped; open question on the SB 24-205 effective date replaced

alternatives: Does the Colorado AI Act apply to any of your AI systems as a developer or deployer of a high-risk AI system, and what documentation will you provide to us as deployer?

question: How do you track new state laws on AI and automated decision-making and assess whether they apply to you or to our use of your service?
business_concern: The state AI law landscape changes quickly.
risk_addressed: Customer adopts a service that becomes non-compliant after a new law.

question: As an insurer, we must oversee third-party AI systems under our AI program. Will you provide documentation, testing information and audit cooperation for AI used in services you provide to us?
business_concern: Insurers adopting the NAIC model bulletin extend AI governance to vendors.
risk_addressed: Insurer unable to demonstrate oversight of vendor AI to its regulator.

question: Do any of your AI features interact directly with people or generate content in a way that triggers EU AI Act transparency duties, and how do you meet them?
business_concern: Users must be told when they interact with AI or see AI-generated content in some cases.
risk_addressed: Non-compliant chat or content features.
regulatory_authority: EU AI Act national market surveillance authorities

history.change: Added SRC-EU-AI-OMNIBUS-2026 and the amended Article 50(2) date in a new scope note

answer_scope_note: Applies only if Echelon places AI systems on the EU market or their output is used in the EU; no EU exposure is established. Under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 50(2) applies from 2026-12-02 to synthetic-content systems placed on the market before 2026-08-02.

question: Does any part of your service produce outputs that we should treat as a model under our model risk management policy, and will you support our validation of it?
alternatives: Provide information sufficient for us to include your models in our model inventory.
Will your models meet our SR 11-7 model risk management requirements?
business_concern: Banks must validate and monitor models they rely on, including vendor models.
risk_addressed: Unvalidated vendor model drives decisions and draws examination findings.

history.change: Replaced superseded SRC-SR-11-7 with SRC-SR-26-2 (SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 and SR 21-8 on 2026-04-17); basis set to reasonably-inferred because the SR 26-2 guidance attachment has not been read; kept SRC-SR-11-7 as informed-by for historical questionnaire wording; added legacy SR 11-7 wording as an alternative; regulatory authority now includes FDIC

answer_scope_note: SR 26-2 (2026-04-17, Federal Reserve, OCC and FDIC) superseded SR 11-7 and SR 21-8; bank questionnaires may still cite SR 11-7, which is kept here as a historical reference. This is supervisory guidance to banks and reaches Echelon only through the bank's contract.

question: Can you provide documentation for independent validation of your models: purpose, design, data, assumptions, limitations, performance testing and monitoring?
business_concern: Validation requires documentation the vendor controls.
risk_addressed: Customer cannot assess conceptual soundness or limitations.

history.change: Replaced superseded SRC-SR-11-7 with SRC-SR-26-2 (SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 and SR 21-8 on 2026-04-17); basis set to reasonably-inferred because the SR 26-2 guidance attachment has not been read; regulatory authority now includes FDIC

question: Do you perform ongoing performance monitoring and outcomes analysis of your models, and will you share the results with us?
business_concern: Model performance drifts after deployment.
risk_addressed: Degraded model performance unnoticed by the relying bank.

history.change: Replaced superseded SRC-SR-11-7 with SRC-SR-26-2 (SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 and SR 21-8 on 2026-04-17); basis set to reasonably-inferred because the SR 26-2 guidance attachment has not been read; regulatory authority now includes FDIC

question: Will you notify us in advance of material changes to models, prompts or AI providers so we can update our model inventory and revalidate?
business_concern: Unannounced changes invalidate prior validation.
risk_addressed: Customer relies on a validation that no longer reflects production behavior.

history.change: Replaced superseded SRC-SR-11-7 with SRC-SR-26-2 (SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 and SR 21-8 on 2026-04-17); basis set to reasonably-inferred because the SR 26-2 guidance attachment has not been read

question: Do you disclose where AI is used in the service you provide and in your own operations, including whether AI writes your software?
alternatives: Is any part of your product developed using generative AI?
Describe how AI is used in delivering your services.
Will you tell us proactively when any service you deliver to us relies on a model or generative AI, and explain how the model works and the basis for its outputs?
business_concern: Customers need truthful disclosure to assess and explain their own AI exposure.
risk_addressed: Undisclosed AI use discovered later undermines trust and compliance.

history.change: Added real-world alternative wording from DD-QNR-001 topic 1 and source reference(s) SRC-Q-MS-MIN-SECURITY-STANDARDS, SRC-Q-FSISAC-GENAI-VENDOR-GUIDE (maps-to)

question: Are AI-generated outputs labeled as such in the product and in communications sent to our donors, advisors or grantees?
business_concern: Recipients should be able to tell AI-generated content from verified facts and human statements.
risk_addressed: Recipients treat AI drafts as authoritative statements by the sponsor.

question: Can we disable AI features for our tenant without losing core functions?
business_concern: Some customers cannot yet approve AI use or need to suspend it during an incident.
risk_addressed: Customer forced to accept AI processing to keep using the service.

question: Will you notify us before introducing new AI features or AI providers that process our data, and can we decline them?
business_concern: Customers want control over new processing of their data.
risk_addressed: New AI processing introduced without customer review.

question: Do you measure or estimate the energy use and environmental footprint of the AI features and AI tools used to deliver the service, and will you disclose it to us?
business_concern: Mission-driven buyers weigh the environmental cost of AI use against their own commitments.
risk_addressed: The customer adopts AI-dependent services whose footprint conflicts with its stated commitments.
